summary: Deletes or retains whole channels and/or samples from a CHOP using name, number, value, constantness, sample comparisons, and scope rules.

key_params.name: scoped
key_params.note: Channel scope used for name-based deletion

key_params.name: firstchan
key_params.note: Use first channel as sample compare source

key_params.name: lastchan
key_params.note: Use last channel as sample compare source

key_concepts: Delete CHOP removes whole channels, individual samples, or both from the input CHOP.
Channel deletion can match by channel name, channel number ranges, value ranges, or constant-valued channels.
Delete and Non-scoped modes choose whether matched channels are removed or retained.
Sample deletion uses one or more compare channels, and deleting a sample index removes that sample from every channel.
When all samples are deleted, the operator keeps one sample and reports a length of one sample.
common_gotchas: Deleting a sample index removes that sample from every channel, not only the compare channel.
If all samples are deleted, the operator keeps one sample and reports length one.
Channel deletion and sample deletion are separate workflows with different parameter pages.
Compare-channel choice is critical for multi-channel data such as RGBA or XYZ position samples.
For simpler channel filtering or interval trimming, Select CHOP, Trim CHOP, or Splice CHOP may be clearer.
